query:
Photographic role: Describe the adult subject's green irises with visible radial fibers and a sharp limbal edge.
Scene context: A close adult portrait; gaze remains a separate choice.

diagnosis.reason: The common pool contains broad iris colors and several owned color-distribution or stylized pattern relations. Reading full canonical native source revealed no corresponding positive green iris plus radial texture/limbal-border option, or resolved collarette, crypt, pigment-fleck and interrupted-furrow meanings. Extra local features are not recoverable from gaze, eyelids or catchlight stock. The unchanged-query baseline returns 0/8 fully matching records and instead exposes gaze, pupil-shape and portrait-composition neighbors; this is consistent with the identified missing local iris meanings.

existing_candidates.limitation: A color label; no radial surface texture or limbal boundary.
No green selection and no local structure.
A broad dark color label; no resolved stromal pattern.

existing_candidates.meaning: a selected color forms a ring immediately around the pupil; the outer part of that same iris carries a different selected color
existing_candidates.limitation: Central color distribution is different from the limbal border or a raised collarette.

existing_candidates.meaning: two or more circular bands share the iris center; the pupil remains distinguishable from the surrounding ring pattern
existing_candidates.limitation: Complete pattern relation, without natural peripheral interrupted surface folds.

existing_candidates.meaning: a small bounded source reflection is visible on the specified corneal surface
existing_candidates.limitation: Corneal light reflection is lighting. It cannot establish intrinsic iris pigment or structure.

existing_candidates.meaning: window reflection visible in the iris
existing_candidates.limitation: Photographic shorthand for a reflection; no evidence for fibers, eye color or iris morphology.

sources.title: MedlinePlus Genetics: Is eye color determined by genetics?
sources.supports: Iris pigmentation surrounds the pupil; eye color varies continuously and green/hazel is a common descriptive category. No genetic or demographic inference is transferred to candidates.

sources.title: Shyu and Wyatt (2009): Appearance of the human eye: optical contributions to the limbal ring
sources.supports: Primary optical experiment supports a substantial optical contribution to the dark outer iris border; visible darkness is not automatically a pigment stripe or a health claim.

sources.title: Edwards et al. (2016): Analysis of iris surface features in populations of diverse ancestry
sources.supports: Primary photographic analysis distinguishes collarette-delimited zones, crypt openings, pigment spots, and interrupted peripheral contraction furrows. Population correlations are excluded from this authoring.

sources.title: Imaging of iris vasculature: current limitations and future perspective (Eye, 2022)
sources.supports: Technical anatomical review identifies visible radial streaks and separates anterior surface features from posterior folds and specialized angiography. A portrait does not demonstrate microscopic fibers or blood flow.

inventory.method: Scanned all positive global document text without tag filtering; inspected 66 iris-related documents through checked BodyReader records and installed canonical native decoding. Separately inspected all 31 eye_detail-tagged records for context. Compared decoded native content for all shared relevant CIDs with working V3 content; no content differences among the 66 common hits. Working lexical inventory includes 76 records; its 10 extras refer to iris in non-primary contexts rather than missing local anatomy.
inventory.note: Text search guided inspection; these counts are not semantic approval, native qualification or exhaustive proof that no differently worded document exists.

confusion_boundaries: Iris color and surface pattern are owned appearance properties; where the eyes point belongs to gaze_target/gaze_engagement and has no required direction here.
Raised or lowered lids, brow/mouth actions and emotional interpretations do not prove iris structure.
Eyeliner, eyeshadow, mascara, false lashes and colored contact accessories have different carriers from the iris. Contact-lens appearance does not establish biology.
The outer limbal border differs from a colored ring directly around the pupil, the collarette within the iris, and circumferential furrows within peripheral iris tissue.
Radial streaks describe visible pattern. Ordinary portrait pixels do not establish microscopic tissue identity, visible internal muscles, vascular flow or tissue histology.
Corneal catchlights can obscure iris features; they belong to reflected-light appearance and do not create iris pigment, tears or an emotional state.
Visible iris color, crypts, rings and flecks support no age, ethnicity, genetic identity, diagnosis, health or personality inference. The request separately declares an adult subject.
All authored options are optional distinct configurations, not a cumulative checklist for every iris. Occluded or insufficiently resolved structure remains unobservable.
recommendations: Add five substantive local appearance choices spanning color/texture and distinct surface components; retain same-eye ownership and narrow effect properties.
Keep the original query bytes fixed for before/after global H-F2 tests. Score green color, radial pattern, outer border and preserved independent gaze separately.
Review each new source in native form before adoption; these research candidates are discovery-only, with no _semantic_evidence, fabricated approval or runtime activation.
Measure whether the baseline retrieves generic colors, heterochromia or catchlights. A high rank for those is not evidence that the complete requested structure exists.

additional_test_intents.role_focus: Describe a few small brown flecks separated by continuous lighter iris color in one adult's eye.
additional_test_intents.scene_context: A close portrait with gaze chosen elsewhere; makeup remains a separate choice.
checks: no central-ring or whole-eye color substitution

baseline_review.judgment: No top8 source supplies green iris color, visible radial local structure and an outer limbal boundary together. Partial existing color options do not occur in top128; their different hue and missing structure mean this absence alone does not justify query/ranking changes.
